answer: Think of an agent economy as an orchard: each tree must be planted, watered, and tended for months before it bears fruit, so a fake identity costs real time and upkeep. A newcomer starts as a faint ember — it can do small jobs, but only a long record of useful, verified work lets it handle valuable transactions. Reputation acts like a prism: every past interaction splits into visible facets, so one identity cannot hide a bad history behind a fresh name, and mass-producing fake agents becomes more expensive than the fraud it enables.
